label: Execution study, not part of the mover-v3 alpha family. The alpha protocol is protocol-core-draft.json (m = 5). This draft uses none of its slots, and its results never open that protocol's holdout. Deferred to v3.1+ with open review findings X2 (no minimum stage length), X3 (trigger-time basis), X4 (asymmetric H6-e eligibility) and X6 (labels undefined for a TOST test); see the README appendix 'Deferred to v3.1+'.
revised_at: 2026-09-24 (round 2: population named as a gated mechanics-only strategy, H6-c restated as descriptive because arm a needs fewer calls by construction, arm a configuration pinned, H6-e unit and trigger strata, GTC and tranche timing, calendar cap, paper smoke test); round 3 on the same day: trigger references per arm plus a common NBBO-bid basis, stop-market OCO leg, intention-to-treat H6-e unit, flat-symbol entry rule, entry cancel timeout and tranche-reject fallback, a pilot-based power precondition, and a disjoint, sealed population); round 4 on the same day: disjointness by a screen that uses no v3 definition, adapter preconditions for transport intents, safety reservations and reconciliation reports, session-based stages, a statistics section, the SIP feed pinned, and a 2-share minimum)
evidence_class: Official broker documentation read on 2026-09-24 plus repository source reads. No native execution, no paper order and no outcome. Paper fills are simulated by Alpaca, so any result is sim-to-paper evidence, not market evidence.
question: Do broker-held exits (Alpaca trailing_stop and OCO) realize exit prices equivalent to client-side exits, relative to the same trigger reference? REST calls per closed position are reported for both arms as a description, not tested.
independence: Engineering, not alpha. This protocol has its own one-test family and its own paper timeline. It uses no slot of the mover-v3 alpha family (protocol-core-draft.json, m = 5; the archived full draft had m = 35), H1-H5 never wait for it, and no result here opens or informs the alpha holdout. Its positions are mechanics-only and follow population.alpha_disjointness; each H6 paper order is logged at order time in the alpha protocol's accrual log (protocol-draft.json chronology.holdout.accrual_exposure), where it counts toward that protocol's 5% contamination cap and its exposure sensitivity.
data_status: gated. H6 has no source of positions today: v3 defines no paper candidate, the v3 edge-shrink term is 0 until a holdout pass (so every alpha-sized position is 0), and this draft creates no order for the test itself. It cannot accrue any closed position until the population below is committed and the preconditions hold.

evidence.status: read on 2026-09-24. trailing_stop (trail_price or trail_percent) and OCO for a held position ('the entry order is already filled, and you can submit the take-profit and stop-loss in one order submission') are documented. Constraints quoted verbatim: 'Trailing stop orders are currently supported only with single orders. However, we plan to support trailing stop as the stop loss leg of bracket/OCO orders in the future.' and 'you would not be able to submit two conditional closing orders since Alpaca's system would view one of the two orders as exceeding the available position quantity'.

evidence.source: adaptive-paper at aa6fc79: exits.py evaluates stop, take-profit (take_profit_fraction) and trailing rules client-side with no resting broker stop; when a rule fires, native_strategy.py (about lines 755-819) sends one DAY limit at limit_price(bid, ask); replace_exit re-prices only an unfilled resting exit, is off by default (runner.py line 323, exits.replace_enabled False; strategies_v1.py exit_replace_enabled False) and is capped at exit_replace_max_attempts = 3; native_adapter.py builds and accepts only LIMIT/DAY orders (lines 344, 354, 368)
evidence.status: repository source read in the round 2 fix

evidence.source: adaptive-paper on origin/main (unchanged in these paths since aa6fc79): transport.normalize_intent rejects any type other than 'limit', any time_in_force other than 'day' and a missing or non-positive limit_price, and allows only whole-share buys; safety.py reserves each sell intent against held quantity minus pending sells (sell_exceeds_owned_unreserved_position) and stores a limit_price per intent, so two OCO legs on tranche P would reserve 2P; native_adapter.order_report hard-codes OrderType.LIMIT and TimeInForce.DAY and parses Price.from_str(row['limit_price']), which fails on a stop-market or trailing_stop order with a null limit price; config.json uses feed 'iex' and max_order_quantity 1 (config-sip.json exists)
evidence.status: repository source read in the round 4 fix

population.rule: positions opened in Alpaca paper by one named mechanics-only strategy and configuration, committed before the freeze, on a committed symbol list of large-cap stocks and ETFs, at a fixed entry quantity of 2 shares (so tranche P and tranche T each hold 1 share at a full fill). It makes no alpha claim and is exempt from edge shrink for that reason. The configuration uses feed 'sip' (as config-sip.json does), max_order_quantity >= 2 and max_order_notional_usd >= 2 x the highest price the symbol list allows; a SIP entitlement check is part of the paper smoke test. An entry whose final filled quantity is below 2 is counted per arm and excluded from H6-e in both arms, and H6-e is also reported by the arm-b order type that triggered.
population.alpha_disjointness: Disjointness uses no mover-v3 definition, so running it computes no v3 membership on holdout-window prices. An H6 entry in symbol x on session s is allowed only if x is on the committed symbol list, the absolute raw close-to-close return of x (split-adjusted daily bars) was below 10% on every session s-5 .. s-1, the latest SIP trade before the entry decision is within 10% of the previous session's split-adjusted close, and the entry is at or after 10:31 ET. A position still open at the close of a session whose absolute raw return reached 10% is closed at the next session's first eligible quote by a client-side exit and counted. Every H6 order is logged at order time in the alpha accrual log (protocol-draft.json chronology.holdout.accrual_exposure), so any residual overlap with v3 D or I trades is identified there after the fact, when the alpha holdout is read, and counts toward its contamination cap.
population.flat_symbol: Alpaca holds one net position per symbol, so an entry in a symbol is sent only when the account is flat in that symbol and has no open order in it (for arm b, after both tranche orders are terminal). Skipped entries are counted per arm. A synthetic test covers a second entry while the first position or a tranche order is open.
population.entry_order: Both arms use the same entry: a DAY limit at limit_price(bid, ask) whose unfilled remainder is cancelled after 30 s (IOC is unverified on the adapter). The position is the filled quantity once the entry is terminal. Arm a's client-side rules are active from the first fill; arm b's tranche orders are sent once the entry is terminal, so arm b has at most 30 s plus the cancel acknowledgement without a price stop, and that interval is reported per position.
population.sealed_ledger: H6 fills and closed positions go to a sealed ledger (sha256 committed per session batch). No per-position exit price or P&L of H6 positions is displayed or computed during a stage; stage statistics are computed only through h6-access-log.jsonl entries.
population.open_decision: Whether such a strategy is compatible with adaptive-paper README's rule 'No strategy manufactures trades to hit a throughput target' needs an explicit, recorded decision before the freeze. If the decision is no, H6 is dropped.
population.rate: estimated before the freeze by a short paper pilot of the committed mechanics-only strategy and configuration (both arms, labelled as measurement, never counted in any stage). The pilot records the exit-type mix per arm and the H6-e-eligible positions per arm per session. If that rate x 126 is below 1.5 x the largest stage minimum (1.5 x 200 = 300 eligible positions per arm), H6 is dropped. Retained adaptive-paper trial ledgers of other strategies are not an estimate of this rate.
population.calendar_cap: each stage has at most 126 sessions (protocol-core-draft.json populations.session_calendar, early closes included); a stage that has not reached its minimum by then is labelled underpowered and the protocol stops

arm_assignment.rule: arm = a if the first byte of sha256('mover-v3-h6|' + symbol + '|' + entry session (YYYY-MM-DD) + '|' + k) is even, else b, where k is the 1-based count of this symbol's entries in this session in decision order
arm_assignment.commit: the assignment is written to the durable order ledger before the entry order is sent. client_order_id is not an input, so the client that generates IDs cannot re-roll an assignment. A position whose ledger assignment is missing or written after the submit is excluded and counted.

a_client.rule: the current exits.py chain on the whole position: triggers are evaluated client-side on the bid (strategies_v1.py: pnl_bps = bid / average_price - 1, trail_bps = bid / high_bid - 1), and a fired rule sends one DAY limit at limit_price(bid, ask), which for a sell is bid - $0.02
a_client.config: exits.replace_enabled = false (the shipped default), so an unfilled exit is not re-priced; exit_replace_max_attempts = 3, exit_replace_tolerance_bps = 0 and exit_replace_min_interval_seconds = 0 are recorded but inactive. Any other setting is a new protocol version.

b_broker.constraint: each share carries at most one broker-held closing order (the documented rule above): a trailing_stop cannot be an OCO leg, and a second conditional closing order on the same shares is rejected as exceeding the available quantity
b_broker.structure: the filled quantity q is split into two tranches. Tranche P (take-profit tranche) = floor(q x f_p) shares, carrying one OCO (take-profit limit at take_profit_bps and a stop-market stop leg, stop_price only and no limit_price, at stop_bps). Tranche T (trailing tranche) = q - P shares, carrying one trailing_stop with trail_percent = effective_trailing_bps at entry / 100, which is also that tranche's only stop. f_p = take_profit_fraction when it is below 1; when take_profit_fraction = 1 (the strategies_v1 default), f_p = 0.5, fixed here. A tranche of 0 shares is not sent, and the whole position carries the other tranche's single order.
b_broker.timing: tranche orders are submitted only once the entry order is terminal (filled, cancelled or expired), sized from the final filled quantity; no top-up for later fills
b_broker.time_in_force: GTC for both tranche orders, so multi-session holds need no daily resubmission. If the paper smoke test shows GTC rejected for an order class, that class uses DAY plus one resubmission per tranche at each session's first eligible quote, and those calls are counted.
b_broker.tranche_reject: If a tranche order is rejected (for example because the price has already crossed its stop level, or as exceeding the available quantity), that tranche falls back to arm a's client-side rule chain for its shares. The position stays in arm b for H6-e (intention to treat), and fallbacks are counted and reported per arm and reason.
b_broker.client_side: time, risk-off, force, quote-stale and halt exits stay client-side. A client-side exit first cancels both tranche orders (one call each), waits for both cancels to be terminal, then sends one closing order for the remaining quantity.
b_broker.difference_from_a: arm b is not a byte-identical copy of arm a's rule chain: tranche T has no separate fixed stop and tranche P no trailing rule, and arm a sells the whole position on take-profit (take_profit_fraction = 1) while arm b sells tranche P. H6-e therefore compares execution quality against each fill's own trigger reference, not P&L, and only for stop-type triggers.

trigger_reference.arm_a: stop_loss: average_price x (1 - effective stop_bps / 1e4); trailing: high_bid x (1 - effective trailing_bps / 1e4), with high_bid as of the trigger tick. Both are the rule's level, not the bid that crossed it.
trigger_reference.arm_b: the order's stop_price at trigger as read from the order or its trade_updates event (for trailing_stop, the stop_price Alpaca reports, with its hwm logged).
trigger_reference.common_basis: for both arms, also the NBBO bid at each arm's trigger timestamp (arm a: the triggering tick; arm b: the trade_updates timestamp of the stop leg's trigger or fill) from the same SIP quote stream (population.rule pins feed 'sip'; on the IEX feed this basis does not exist). H6-e is computed on the per-arm reference and on this common basis; both are reported, and a pass requires both.
trigger_reference.trigger_basis_check: The round 3 review found that the cited orders-at-alpaca page does not state which price series triggers a stop or trailing_stop (last trade, bid or NBBO); this round did not reopen the page. The paper smoke test records the trigger basis; if it cannot be determined, H6-e uses the common basis only.

shadow: for each position, the other arm's trigger time and reference price are computed from the same quote stream for paired diagnostics, never traded

call_count_description.arm_a: 2 calls per closed position at a full fill (entry plus one exit limit), plus the entry cancel when the entry is not filled in 30 s. With replace disabled no further calls are made; an unfilled exit expires at the close and is handled by the existing recovery path, whose calls are counted.
call_count_description.arm_b: 3 calls when broker legs close the position (entry, OCO, trailing_stop; 2 when a tranche is empty), 6 when closed client-side (plus 2 cancels and 1 closing order), plus any DAY resubmissions
call_count_description.consequence: arm b needs more calls than arm a by construction (3 + 3s against about 2), so the previous test 'arm b uses at least 2x fewer calls' could not pass and is withdrawn. The call counts per closed position, the realized client-closed share s and any resubmissions are reported per arm as a description only.

primary_tests.unit: intention to treat: one closed position whose first fired exit is stop-type (arm a: the stop_loss or trailing rule fires first; arm b: the OCO stop leg or the trailing_stop triggers first). Its value is the quantity-weighted mean, over every fill that closes the shares covered by that trigger (arm a: the whole position; arm b: the triggering tranche, the other tranche being excluded from the value), of (fill price - trigger_reference) / trigger_reference in bps, whichever order closes them: the exit limit, the recovery path, a time exit or a next-session close. Positions whose first fired exit is a take-profit or a client-side rule are excluded from H6-e, counted and reported by trigger type. Arm a's stop exit is a DAY limit at bid - $0.02 that can rest unfilled; intention to treat keeps those positions at their final realized close, so the arm is not censored to filled limits.
primary_tests.statistic: median of the position values, arm b minus arm a
primary_tests.p_value: p = max(p_lower, p_upper), the larger of the two one-sided bootstrap p-values, as statistics.tost_p defines them

descriptive: H6-c: log(mean REST calls per closed position, arm a / arm b), with a bootstrap interval; no pass rule
stop-exit fill rate and time from trigger to final close, per arm
H6-e restricted to positions whose first stop-type exit order filled (the censored comparison), as a sensitivity
take-profit fills: the same statistic, reported separately
paired shadow differences per trigger type
also_not_supported_if: any paper partial-fill, trigger-price or trigger-reference behaviour that departs from the documented semantics, a trigger basis that the smoke test cannot determine and that differs between arms on the common basis, or any rejection of a tranche order as exceeding the available quantity (recorded per event)

multiple_testing.procedure: TOST (two one-sided tests, each at alpha 0.05) at validation and at the holdout; no multiplicity adjustment with m = 1
multiple_testing.development_screen: unadjusted p <= 0.05 with the development sample; nominates for validation only

stages.order: Stages are cut by session, not per arm. A stage starts at the session after the previous stage's end (the first session with an entry, for development) and ends at the close of the first session on which both arms have reached the stage minimum of H6-e-eligible closed positions. Every eligible position closed within that session range belongs to the stage for both arms, so both arms cover the same calendar period; the per-arm counts and any imbalance are reported. Positions open at a stage's end belong to the stage in which they close.
stages.development: minimum 100 eligible closed positions per arm
stages.holdout: minimum 200 per arm, read only if H6-e passed validation, with an access log entry in blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/h6-access-log.jsonl committed before the read
stages.minimum: a stage that has not reached its minimum in both arms within population.calendar_cap is underpowered and cannot pass
stages.note: prospective paper only; disjoint from every historical window and independent of the alpha protocol's stages

power.median_efficiency: standard error of a median difference taken as sigma x sqrt(2/n) x sqrt(pi/2) (normal approximation)
power.development: n = 100 per arm, alpha 0.05: SE 8.9 bps, TOST interval half-width 14.6 bps, equivalence passes if the observed difference is within +/-10.4 bps, power about 0.76 at a true difference of 0
power.validation_and_holdout: n = 200 per arm, alpha 0.05 (m = 1): SE 6.3 bps, half-width 10.3 bps, passes within +/-14.7 bps, power about 0.98 at a true difference of 0
power.previous_drafts: 40 / 60 / 150 per arm at 0.05/37 could not pass by construction; the round 1 draft used alpha 0.025 for a two-test family whose call-count test could not pass

statistics.unit_and_resampling: circular session block bootstrap over the stage's sessions in date order, block length 5 sessions, B = 100,000; each draw resamples sessions jointly for both arms (the stage covers the same sessions for both, stages.order) and recomputes the median of each arm's position values and their difference, arm b minus arm a
statistics.generator: numpy.random.Generator(PCG64) seeded per stage with numpy.random.SeedSequence(entropy = the first 8 bytes of sha256(frozen H6 protocol id) read big-endian, spawn_key = (stage_index,)), stage_index 0 development, 1 validation, 2 holdout
statistics.tost_p: with d_b the bootstrap differences in bps and margin 25 bps: p_lower = (1 + #{b : d_b <= -25}) / (B + 1) and p_upper = (1 + #{b : d_b >= +25}) / (B + 1); p = max(p_lower, p_upper), and equivalence passes when p <= 0.05, which is the percentile 90% interval lying inside +/-25 bps
statistics.evaluator: the H6 evaluator is committed with synthetic tests (a known equivalent pair, a known shifted pair, the seed derivation and the session-cut stages) before any stage read

outcome_reporting: the three labels of protocol-core-draft.json outcome_reporting (a stage-specific pass label; not supported with the excluded size stated; underpowered)
sizing: the fixed entry quantity of 2 shares of the mechanics-only strategy (population.rule)
freeze_preconditions: An independent pre-outcome review from a different session and model family, findings resolved in a dated record
The mechanics-only strategy, its configuration and notional committed, and the no-manufactured-trades decision recorded (population.open_decision)
The paper pilot run and its exit-type mix and eligible-position rate recorded, with H6 dropped if the rate misses population.rate's bound

Adapter paths for OCO and trailing_stop committed with synthetic tests, including a test that one share never carries two closing orders and a test that a client-side exit waits for cancel acknowledgements before its closing order

The same order classes carried through every layer that today accepts only DAY limits, each with synthetic tests: transport.normalize_intent (stop-market, trailing_stop and OCO intents, GTC, no limit_price where the order has none); safety.py reservations and caps priced from the stop price or trail reference, with an OCO's two legs reserving its tranche once, so the pair never raises sell_exceeds_owned_unreserved_position; and native_adapter order_report and reconciliation for non-limit, GTC and OCO-leg orders with a null limit_price, including a startup reconciliation that meets an open trailing_stop and open OCO legs
The mechanics-only configuration pinned to feed 'sip', with max_order_quantity >= 2, and the SIP entitlement confirmed in the paper smoke test
The H6 evaluator committed with its synthetic tests (statistics.evaluator)

A paper mechanics smoke test of the tranche pair (one OCO with a stop-market leg plus one trailing_stop on split tranches of one position, GTC), labelled as measurement, with its result recorded, including the trigger price series Alpaca uses (trigger_reference.trigger_basis_check) and a tranche rejection after the stop level is crossed
Synthetic tests for the flat-symbol rule, the 30 s entry cancel before tranche submission, the tranche-reject fallback and alpha_disjointness
The arm-assignment ledger write tested to precede the entry submit
